concepts.title: The Notion of Letter-Numbers
concepts.definition: A letter-number is a letter that stands for any number of a set: writing 3n for three times a number lets one short rule speak for hundreds of number facts at once.
concepts.key_idea: Letters give numbers a costume that fits every case: one letter-expression stores a whole table of results.

concepts.title: Evaluating Letter-Number Expressions
concepts.definition: To evaluate an expression like 3n + 2, replace the letter with the given number and carry out the operations in order; different values of n give different values of the expression.
concepts.key_idea: Substitute, then obey the order of operations: the letter is a placeholder waiting for its number.

concepts.title: Rules and Patterns as Expressions
concepts.definition: Patterns become portable when written with letter-numbers: the perimeter of a square is 4s for any side s, and a matchstick pattern growing by a fixed step becomes an expression in the figure number.
concepts.key_idea: A letter-expression is a pattern you can carry: it answers not one question but every question of a family.

concepts.title: Simplifying Letter-Number Expressions
concepts.definition: Expressions with the same letter-numbers combine: 3a + 2a becomes 5a, and 4b + 3 becomes shorter forms only when like parts are joined, keeping the value unchanged for every number.
concepts.key_idea: Like parts add, unlike parts wait: simplification shortens the expression without touching its value.
